# White Knuckle City

> "White Knuckle City" is a nickname and love letter for Cleveland, Ohio and its
> three major pro sports teams — the Guardians (MLB), Browns (NFL), and Cavaliers
> (NBA). It captures the white-knuckle tension of following Cleveland sports, where
> the lead is never safe and games go down to the final out or whistle.

## Key facts

- **What it is:** A nickname for Cleveland, Ohio, describing what it feels like to root for its teams.
- **Why the name:** Decades of tense, heartbreaking finishes — Red Right 88 (1981), The Drive (1987), The Fumble (1988), The Shot (1989), the 1997 World Series Game 7, and the 2016 Indians Game 7 loss — alongside the euphoric 2016 Cavaliers championship (a 3–1 comeback over a 73-win Warriors team).
- **The teams:** Cleveland Guardians (MLB), Cleveland Browns (NFL), Cleveland Cavaliers (NBA).
- **The White Knuckle Index:** A live tension meter on the site that reads current Cleveland game scores from public ESPN scoreboards and rates the moment from 0 (relaxed) to 100 (maximum grip), refreshing every 60 seconds.
- **Location:** Cleveland, Ohio (the 216).
- **Affiliation:** Independent fan project. Not affiliated with any team, league, or broadcaster.
